utterances.text: -1, as we did it. And the English version, therefore, A-1, and the B/C/S version B-1. And it follows that the other sheet of paper, to be as neutral as possible, gets B-2 in B/C/S and A-2 in English. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For us, it's not possible to see what's the source of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think as regards the letter, the objections are, in substance, the same as yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And as regards the first announcement, can we hear something from the OTP, indicating that what one probably can read already from Exhibit Number 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It indicates that it was seized from the Municipal Assembly building in 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Without additional source, just as the outclip of a newspaper, and nobody knows what newspaper this is. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then being aware of the limited -- probably limited value of such a piece of evidence, it is admitted under the numbers as indicated before. Document 268, now 83. We discussed already that there are several sides of Kozarski Vjesnik, due to the fact that photocopies in A4 were taken from the entire page. So any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This interview has never been authorised, Your Honour. And it does not reflect the authorisation, either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is an objection to the content. But as a document, it should be admitted into evidence. Of course, it has to be debated and discussed what it's about with the contents of this document and on the authenticity, no doubt. But then it's admitted into evidence as S83A and B. Turning now to 278, we face some problems because it seems to be the same document as we have it under... Wait a minute. It's the former 279. Seems to be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears to me that two separate pieces of paper were seized during the same search from the same location. That's why they have two different ERN numbers. And actually, although it's -- the typewriting appears to be the same, the handwriting in the upper right appears to be different. I can withdraw, for the purposes of clarity, I can withdraw the 279. I won't offer that into evidence, if there's a challenge to the authenticity and it's somehow relevant, we can reoffer it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Signature on this document is completely illegible, so we can't even confirm it or... But to be cautious enough, we object to this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then following this policy as regards this aspect, document with 65 ter number 278 is admitted into evidence as 84A in English and 84B in B/C/S. And 279, it was withdrawn. And thereby, nothing has to be admitted into evidence. It is not tendered by the Defence, as I understand correctly. Not to confuse our numbers, we should maintain the old numbers and, therefore, have no 85 at all. Let's then proceed to 299 where we actually have the problem that the B/C/S version appears twice with different numbers. I can't identify the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Two pieces of paper were seized from the same location, probably back to back, from the numbering. So the same document was just -- they seized both pieces of paper. And looking at the print, it appears that one was a copy of the other because the first one clearly has a better-quality print, I believe, than the second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can we proceed in the same way as regards the last document, withdraw one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, although that may be a little confusing since they only have one number at the moment. You want me to withdraw just the ERN number of 00633790, yes, I will withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections to the remaining parts?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document, it's not clear whether we had a Crisis Staff with War Presidency at the same time, so we object to this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Nevertheless admitted into evidence under 86A, and the former document ending with the number 89 is now 86B. And the other piece of paper is withdrawn. Turning now to 303, objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We really cannot identify the document. No seal, no signature, so just to be on the same side as previously, we object to this document also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then this is admitted into evidence as 87A and B. 305, if you could just assist us which part of the document. It reads as if it would be Kozarski Vjesnik. It's translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think Mr. Lukic could probably help us with that. I think it's the one on the right-hand side on the top, top right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't try. I should not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the top one actually. In the middle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Then the translation is admitted into evidence as S88A, and the article in the middle of the page, top and in the middle of this page, 88B in B/C/S. Then 365. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. No signature --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Oh --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think we have 306.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 306, sorry. First 306.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 306, it's the same article, the same page from the papers. Maybe another article. I'll just check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now the article is on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then former 306 goes. The English translation admitted into evidence as 89A, and then the following page number ending with 83, the article on the top right-hand side as 89B. Then 365.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We object to this one as well. No signature appears on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG

utterances.text: I think yesterday we gave it to you. Ms. Karper wrote it down with you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would it be agreed between the parties that we leave these additional signatures for Monday? Mr. Lukic, do you have possibility to meet your client during the weekend?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we don't, Your Honour. We cannot visit our client during the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think the dispute is pretty clear already with the numbers that we have gone through, and the way I understand it is the signatures that Your Honour described as Milomir, I'm not sure I can read that, the Defence is denying. Or Mr. Lukic is denying. One thing I want clear is whether what that denial has. That's not evidence. Your Honour indicated that there is a possibility open to the Defence of some procedure to have the accused testify, which we would welcome, because we want to cross-examine him on that issue if there's going to be any evidentiary value given to that by counsel. We're confident that's his signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I believe it wouldn't be fair to request an answer late Friday evening on such an important question, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Until now, our standpoint was that our client would not testify. I don't know. It might change, but I doubt it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I indicated earlier that there were several possibilities. You took one possibility out of these, of course. But I have to recall that in this Trial Chamber, it is the right of the accused, in any appropriate point of time, to take the floor and to make a statement if he so wants. Notwithstanding, of course, his right to remain silent. But if he wants to take the floor, Dr. Stakic you may know that you have this right and you may exercise this right in this Tribunal. But I think it -- as mentioned, it wouldn't be fair to go into details of this part. If the Defence wants to make any additional remarks to the list of documents I mentioned before and the signatures provided by -- it will probably once again provided by the OTP, then please feel free to do so not later than Wednesday next week. I hope that you will have time to visit your client until then. Any other observations for today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just very briefly. If the Defence decides to leave the matter as it now stands, we would very strongly argue that the denial, there is no denial in evidence, that there is absolutely no evidentiary value to counsel. I mean, I appreciate focussing on the issue, but there's no evidentiary value to counsel making a statement, "this is not my client's signature" because under the rules, evidence comes from witnesses, not from counsel, any more than my making the statement that it is his signature is evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We may exchange our different views on this possibly later on. And as I said already, the Trial Chamber is grateful for the contributions given by the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, only one remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I cannot meet my client next week either because we are in the trial the whole day, from the morning until the afternoon. So we might use that lunch break maybe. I don't know if it would be sufficient, sufficiently long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Probably we'll give you the possibility by having a longer break, if necessary and if helpful in the interests of justice. I can't see any other requests. And thereby, we conclude our today's session and we meet again Monday morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 6.57 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 10th day of June, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
